recent_articles.title: NFHS-6 data on child nutrition carries sobering warnings | The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **NFHS-6** data reveals mixed results on child nutrition in India. While stunting has declined nationally, severe wasting and underweight prevalence remain concerning.  Several large states have seen deterioration in these areas, including Jharkhand, UP, and Rajasthan.  Exclusive breastfeeding rates have also fallen sharply in some states, raising concerns about the effectiveness of postnatal support programs. Despite progress in vaccination coverage, the decline in breastfeeding and continued high levels of wasting and underweight suggest that more needs to be done to address these issues.

recent_articles.title: DMK absent, allies restive, INDIA bloc braces for a difficult conversation at today’s meeting | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express

recent_articles.title: Nitin Nabin instructs BJP cadre in Jharkhand to gear up for 2029 Assembly election - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: India Youth Not Puppets Of Some People On Foreign Soil, BJP Chief Nitin Nabin

recent_articles.title: Lodhi Crematorium wall collapse: As a labourer dies, a family loses its home | Delhi News - The Indian Express

The deceased laborer was identified as Rahul Kharwan, while injured laborers Rajesh (48) and Umar (20) are receiving treatment. The police, fire department, and ambulance personnel conducted a joint rescue operation before securing the site.

recent_articles.title: Why Kodagu homestay worker was denied bail in US tourist assault case

recent_articles.title: Pseudo-police gang that kidnapped businessman and extorted ₹5.26 lakh busted in Cyberabad - The Hindu

Police are continuing to investigate and identify additional victims.

recent_articles.title: As El Niño threatens monsoon, farmer groups promote millets, mulching and drip irrigation | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union Ministry of Agriculture** is working to support farmers facing challenges from a weak southwest monsoon by promoting drought-resistant crops and climate-resilient farming practices. The ministry has identified **farmer-producer organizations (FPOs)** across the country that are cultivating drought-resistant crops like millets, and is holding webinars to educate farmers on these methods.  **The Ministry** plans to use the network of over 63 lakh farmers from 10,000 FPOs to encourage adoption of climate-resilient practices, including alternative crops and moisture conservation techniques.

recent_articles.title: High-Speed Chase Then A Farzi-Style Move: How UP Drug Smugglers Tried To Escape Cops, Sonebhadra

The smugglers rammed a police vehicle and attempted to distract officers with the money before being apprehended.  The **SOG** personnel used a local's car to continue the pursuit and eventually stopped the smugglers. During the operation, one smuggler was injured and arrested, while authorities recovered 3 kg of opium, 225 kg of poppy husk, and Rs 50,000 in cash.

recent_articles.title: How runaway tigress’s cubs could save Similipal’s big cat population | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Zeenat**, a tigress relocated from the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra, gave birth to four cubs in **Similipal Tiger Reserve** in Odisha. This marks a significant milestone for conservation efforts as it diversifies the gene pool of Similipal's tigers and addresses concerns about inbreeding.  The translocation program was initiated to introduce fresh genetic material into the population, aiming to improve the long-term survival of the reserve's tigers. **Prakash Chand Gogineni**, Field Director of **Similipal Tiger Reserve**, stated that the cubs are expected to have a broader genetic base and contribute to securing the future of Similipal's tiger population.  The birth has prompted discussions on whether Zeenat's radio collar should be removed once the cubs begin moving independently.

recent_articles.title: Tigress Zeenat gives birth to four cubs in Similipal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Odisha** Chief Minister Mohan Majhi announced that tigress Zeenat, relocated from Maharashtra's Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in 2025, has given birth to four cubs in Similipal Tiger Reserve.  The successful birth is a significant achievement for the state's wildlife conservation efforts and signifies an increase in tiger population. **Zeenat** had previously faced challenges during her acclimatization period but was successfully reintroduced with support from the **National Tiger Conservation Authority**. The success of this translocation effort, especially after previous attempts in Satkosia Tiger Reserve failed, emphasizes the importance of habitat protection and genetic diversity for tigers.

recent_articles.title: Tana Bhagats of Jharkhand and their opposition of a highway project
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatmala** scheme's highway project in Jharkhand is facing protests from the Tana Bhagat community, who claim it violates their land rights and ancestral sites protected under special Constitutional provisions. The project aims to widen NH-43 between Gumla and Chhattisgarh, a part of the Raipur-Dhanbad Economic Corridor.  The **Jharkhand** government has defended its actions, stating that the acquisition is being carried out under the National Highways Act, 1956, while local activists claim religious sites are affected. The project's completion will significantly reduce travel time between the two states and provide faster connectivity to industrial hubs.

recent_articles.title: CBSE Chairman, Secretary Transferred, Panel Formed To Probe Irregularities In On-Screen Marking System
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Singh** and **Himanshu Gupta**, the Chairman and Secretary of the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)**, have been transferred following controversy surrounding the On-screen Marking System (OSM). A one-member committee led by Ms. S Radha Chauhan will investigate irregularities including answer sheet mix-ups, evaluation errors, and misallocated grades. The CBSE's tender process for OSM has also come under scrutiny after concerns were raised about technical issues and payment failures.  The controversy was amplified in Parliament where Opposition leaders accused the board of fraud, prompting a parliamentary panel to investigate.

recent_articles.title: Five new Supreme Court judges sworn in - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** of India received five new judges on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, bringing its total to 37. The appointments were made following the Union government's approval of recommendations from the collegium headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant.  The new judges include former Chief Justices of various High Courts and Senior Advocate V.S. Mohana, who becomes only the second woman to be elevated directly from the Bar to the Supreme Court. These additions aim to address the court’s backlog of over 93,000 cases and facilitate regular Constitution Bench convenings.  The appointments are part of a larger effort by the CJI to reduce the pendency of cases before the court.

recent_articles.title: Five new Supreme Court judges sworn in - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** of India welcomed five new judges on Tuesday, June 2nd, 2026, increasing its total strength to 37.  These appointments follow the Union government's increase in sanctioned judges from 33 to 37, aimed at addressing a backlog of over 93,000 cases. The newly appointed judges include **Sheel Nagu**, former Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court; **Shree Chandrashekhar**, former Chief Justice of Bombay High Court; **Sanjeev Sachdeva**, former Chief Justice of Madhya Pradesh High Court; **Arun Palli**, former Chief Justice of High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh; and Senior Advocate **V.S. Mohana**.  The appointments are part of a larger effort to balance regional representation and improve gender diversity on the Bench, as well as address the court's backlog of cases.

recent_articles.title: BJP picks old RSS hand Nagendra Nath Tripathi for outreach to ‘neglected’ Sangh Parivar elders | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express

recent_articles.title: Delhi crime rate against women highest in 2024, Jaipur tops cities - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Delhi** recorded the highest crime rate against women in India in 2024, with a rate of 130.7 cases per lakh women, according to the **National Crime Records Bureau**.  The city was followed by Telangana, Odisha, Haryana, and Rajasthan.  While some states saw declines in crime rates against women between 2020 and 2024, including Assam, Telangana experienced a significant increase. **Jaipur** reported the highest crime rate among surveyed cities at 199.6 cases per lakh women, while **Chennai** had one of the lowest rates.  Major crimes against women declined in 2024, with decreases seen in cruelty by husbands or relatives, kidnapping and abduction, assaults on women, and dowry-related crimes.

recent_articles.title: Former ED special director Satyabrata Kumar who probed Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya, takes VRS | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Satyabrata Kumar**, a former special director of the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)**, has opted for voluntary retirement from government service after nearly 12 years with the agency.  Kumar oversaw high-profile investigations including those involving Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya, and the Mahadev online betting network. He received approval for voluntary retirement in April and his departure marks the second instance within a year of a senior ED officer leaving government service shortly after exiting the agency. The **ED** arrested Satinder Singh Bhasin, director of Bhasin Infotech and Infrastructure Pvt Ltd, on charges of money laundering related to alleged cheating of home buyers.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi Spotlights Odisha’s Bela Pana & Suvarnarekha In Praise Of Traditional Summer Drinks & Mangoes | OdishaBytes

He mentioned popular beverages like lassi in Punjab and Haryana, chaas in Rajasthan and Gujarat, sattu sharbat in Bihar and Jharkhand, kokum sharbat in Konkan and Goa, panakam, neer mor, and sambar in South India, and bel pana in Odisha. **Modi** also praised the efforts of mango growers, noting that mangoes are a beloved seasonal treat enjoyed across India and globally.

recent_articles.title: BJP Core Group Meet At PM Modi's Residence Today, Rajya Sabha Polls On Agenda

The meeting will focus on finalizing candidates for these elections, which are scheduled for June 18th, as well as strategizing for the high-stakes Rajya Sabha polls following the recent defeat of the Women's reservation bill.  The party also plans to discuss strengthening its organization, mobilizing supporters, and highlighting achievements of the Modi government over the past twelve years.

recent_articles.title: How Pakistan's Social Media Star Shahzad Bhatti Became ISI's New Weapon
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Shahzad Bhatti**, a Pakistani social media influencer linked to the **ISI**, is at the center of a major crackdown by Indian security agencies.  Bhatti's network, which recruits vulnerable youth through social media, allegedly involves criminal activity, radicalization, and plans for attacks on police personnel and sensitive locations. The Delhi Police Special Cell arrested eight suspects connected to Bhatti's module, recovering weapons and explosives. Investigations also reveal links to the **Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan** and a network of violent crimes in Punjab, including the grenade attack on a YouTuber.  Bhatti faces multiple investigations and threats from rival gangs like the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, highlighting his complex role in India's security landscape.

recent_articles.title: The political economy of cash transfers
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** budgetary allocation for unconditional cash transfers (UCT) has increased significantly, reaching 0.9% of GDP in 2026.  While **Government of India** officials and researchers warn that this expansion will increase future debt burdens and crowd out productive investment, the practice persists due to political incentives. The rise of UCT is driven by voter-targeted cash transfers, which have become a popular strategy for election campaigns. This trend has led to increased competition among parties, with promises of cash transfers becoming a key electoral tool.  However, critics argue that poorly designed UCT schemes fail to create long-term productive assets and can negatively impact fiscal sustainability.

recent_articles.title: Over 20% of Indian women suffer marital violence despite increased online engagement: Survey
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of the **National Family Health Survey** revealed that despite social progress, 20% of Indian women marry before age 18 and nearly a third lack access to family planning.  Sexual violence against married women by their spouses remains prevalent at 22.3%, though it has decreased from NFHS-5 (29.2%). **Karnataka** saw the most significant drop in sexual violence, while **Kerala** experienced a rise in the prevalence of this abuse. The survey also highlighted increased internet and cell phone usage among women nationwide, as well as higher bank account ownership and employment rates.

recent_articles.title: 4 Pakistan-made grenades recovered as Delhi Police bust ISI–Mumbai underworld module - The Tribune
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Delhi Police** Special Cell have arrested eight individuals, including three from Punjab, in connection with an alleged Pakistan-linked ISI-Mumbai underworld module. The operation uncovered plans for attacks in Delhi and Mumbai, leading to the recovery of four live hand grenades and 25 cartridges manufactured by the **Pakistan Ordnance Factory**.  The suspects allegedly conducted reconnaissance at several locations, including the Dadar railway station area, and used social media platforms for recruitment and coordination. Investigations are ongoing to trace the wider network of this module.

recent_articles.title: Extremely Severe Alert on phones: Loud alarm warns of bad weather in Delhi NCR — ‘such alert for basic thunderstorm’ | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued an "Extremely Severe Alert" on Saturday evening warning of severe thunderstorms and rainfall across Delhi-NCR and other parts of India. The alert, which was sent via a cell broadcast system, was intended to warn citizens of imminent, life-threatening disasters such as cyclones and heavy rainfall. While some praised the initiative, others questioned the severity of the alert for what they considered moderate weather conditions.  The IMD also issued district-wise nowcast warnings predicting thunderstorms with gusty winds up to 100 kmph in several states.

recent_articles.title: Rare 'intensive' revision in Bihar four months before polls - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** has ordered a special summary revision of electoral rolls in Bihar, marking a departure from its usual practice.  This revision differs from previous intensive revisions by utilizing the 2002-03 electoral roll as a base and incorporating a new pre-printed enumeration form for house-to-house verification. The ECI's decision to conduct this revision ahead of the assembly elections in October 2025 is unusual, as it has rarely ordered full state-wide intensive revisions so far out from the scheduled polls.  This move follows a pattern of the ECI conducting 'intensive' revision in specific areas of states based on various factors like population changes or electoral irregularities.

recent_articles.title: Is Rs 5 crore enough for NRIs to return to India from the US? Former Meta techie who moved to Bengaluru says 'don't chase...' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hemant Pandey**, a former **Meta** employee, returned to India after eight years in the US due to dissatisfaction with H-1B visa restrictions. He now works remotely for **LinkedIn** from Bengaluru and believes earning one-third of his US income is sufficient to live comfortably in India.  Pandey emphasizes that individual circumstances, such as family needs and financial goals, should guide decisions about returning to India rather than focusing on a specific amount of money.

recent_articles.title: Congress holds talks with Hemant Soren on fielding party nominee from one of 2 Rajya Sabha seats going to polls in Jharkhand - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Heatwave eases briefly in Andhra Pradesh, severe conditions likely to return on May 28 - The Hindu

State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA)** warned that severe heatwave conditions are expected to return in over 100 mandals across several districts on Thursday and Friday. The weather activity is influenced by a trough extending from north Bihar to south Telangana, along with an upper air cyclonic circulation persisting over the north Tamil Nadu coast.

recent_articles.title: ‘Come back, my son’: Indian exam leak leaves trail of death, despair, anger | Education News | Al Jazeera

The NTA has acknowledged shortcomings and announced new exam dates, but experts argue that limited resources and outsourcing have contributed to vulnerabilities.  Students like Harsh Dubey and Ritik Mishra, who died by suicide after the cancellation, highlight the devastating impact of the system's failures on aspiring medical professionals.

recent_articles.title: Scorching days, restless nights: Heatwave tightens grip across parts of India - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: JMM, Cong. bid to divide society, undermine tribal rights won’t succeed: BJP - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: 12 MPs, four Parliamentary panels selected for Sansad Ratna Awards - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: A.P. continues to grapple with intense heat as 95 mandals record above 42°C - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andhra Pradesh** continues to experience intense heat, with 95 out of 688 mandals recording temperatures above 42°C. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts that weather systems brewing over the Bay of Bengal may bring isolated showers with lightning and thunderstorms in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema next week, but this activity is not expected to be widespread.

recent_articles.title: Sebi bars seven entities in social media stock recommendations, alleges Rs 58 crore gains - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sebi**, India's market regulator, has accused seven individuals and a group of entities, including Rohan Gupta and Sharon Gupta, of manipulating stock prices through social media influence. The regulator found a significant increase in trade value and profits for the group during the examination period.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Field visits for house-listing, household data collection begin in Jharkhand - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jharkhand** began the first phase of its 2027 Census on May 16, 2026. The incident occurred in Jharkhand and led to doctors removing painkillers due to potential organ impact. The CRPF has seen at least 50 personnel lose limbs since 2015, prompting concerns about career stagnation for security force officials. **Amit Shah**, the Union Home Minister, announced a goal of eradicating Left Wing Extremism by March 31, 2026, leading to increased anti-Maoist operations. Retired CAPF personnel and opposition parties oppose a bill that would reserve key positions in the **Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF)** for IPS officers on deputation.

recent_articles.title: Coal India to set up 8 new coking coal washeries spending ₹3,300 crore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Coal India**, the state-owned miner, plans to invest ₹3,300 crores in building eight new coking coal washeries with a combined capacity of 21.5 million tonnes per year. The expansion will be undertaken by **Central Coalfields Ltd.** and **Bharat Coking Coal Ltd.**, aiming to improve domestic coking coal quality and reduce reliance on imports.  The miner also plans to modernize existing facilities, bringing the total washing capacity to 18.35 million tonnes annually. India currently relies heavily on imports for its coking coal needs, despite having substantial reserves.

recent_articles.title: 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election will be a close battle, says P. Chidambaram - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming 2026 Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly election is expected to be a close contest between two strong fronts, the DMK-Congress alliance and the AIADMK. Veteran Congress leader P. Chidambaram believes that while the BJP will try to influence the election, the DMK alliance will ultimately secure a comfortable majority. He acknowledges the potential for a hung assembly with Vijayakanth's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam potentially impacting the outcome but predicts the DMK alliance will form the government.

recent_articles.title: Jaishankar defends India’s stand as Opposition targets govt. on ‘Pak. mediation’ in West Asia - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **S. Jaishankar**, **External Affairs Minister**, stated that **Pakistan** has been acting as a mediator in U.S.-Iran relations since 1981, calling it a "dalal" and asserting India's strategic interests require maintaining a balanced position despite criticism from the Opposition.  The meeting addressed concerns about India's silence on Iran's attack on West Asian countries, the timing of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**'s visit to Tel Aviv, and Pakistan's role in mediating between the U.S. and Iran. The meeting also saw questions regarding India's commitment to the Non-Aligned Movement and its economic implications from the ongoing crisis.

recent_articles.title: Lone rangers flex their muscle against alliances in Assam battle - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF)** and **United People’s Party Liberation (UPPL)** are confident about their performance in the upcoming Assam Assembly elections, with both parties aiming to significantly increase their seat share.  These non-aligned parties have been gaining momentum as the election date approaches, potentially disrupting the anticipated straight fight between the Bharatiya Janata Party-led NDA and the Congress-led ASM. The AIUDF, which won 16 seats in 2021, is contesting most of its seats in Muslim-dominated areas, while the UPPL, which won six seats in 2021, is contesting more seats outside its core area.  Other non-aligned parties include the Trinamool Congress, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, Aam Aadmi Party, and the National People’s Party.

recent_articles.title: Organisational changes are being made to reach every part of India, says Sunil Ambekar of RSS - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The RSS, celebrating its 100th anniversary, maintains its core ideology of a Hindu nation where Hindutva is understood as a way of life. The organization continues to expand its reach through shakhas and provincial units, addressing issues like demographic change, cross-border infiltration, and population imbalance.  While the Sangh views these concerns as national security threats, it also acknowledges the right of citizens to express dissatisfaction through peaceful means. The organization supports the government's stance on international conflicts while emphasizing a commitment to truth and people's welfare.  The Sangh believes that young people in India are aspirational and focused on contributing to the nation's growth, while acknowledging that some incidents involving religious practices may be perceived as issues of public order.

recent_articles.title: Jharkhand Police seek army help to defuse suspected WWII-era bomb - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jharkhand Police** have requested assistance from the **Indian Army** to defuse a suspected World War II-era unexploded bomb found along the Subarnarekha river. The bomb detection and disposal squad (BDDS) from Ranchi deemed the device "active" and heavy, requiring expertise beyond their capabilities for safe disposal.  The police have cordoned off the area and warned villagers to avoid contact with the object.

recent_articles.title: Without nature, human life is unimaginable, says Hemant Soren on Sharhul - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hemant Soren**, **Jharkhand Chief Minister**, participated in the Sarhul festival in Ranchi on Saturday, March 21, 2026.  He performed prayers and rituals, emphasizing the importance of preserving traditional customs and the deep connection between humans and nature. Mr. Soren also expressed his belief that safeguarding nature is essential for human survival. The **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)** president highlighted the significance of festivals like Sarhul in reminding people of their dependence on nature.

recent_articles.title: EC forms 19 appellate tribunals in West Bengal for appeals on electoral rolls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (EC)** has established 19 Appellate Tribunals in West Bengal to address disputed voter registration appeals. The tribunals, led by former judges, will handle over 60 lakh cases that were rejected by judicial officers during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. This move comes amid concerns about pending adjudication cases and potential disenfranchisement of voters before the upcoming Assembly elections on April 23 and 29.  The EC has also received a Supreme Court order to use former judges in these tribunals, but no supplementary voter lists have been published despite the completion of the final list on February 28.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court quashes copyright case against filmmaker Sujoy Ghosh over his 'Kahaani 2' film - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** ruled in favor of filmmaker **Sujoy Ghosh**, quashing the proceedings against him in a copyright infringement case related to his movie "Kahaani 2". The court found that the lower courts' orders were invalid and set aside, allowing Ghosh's challenge to a Jharkhand High Court order. **Umesh Prasad Mehta**, the complainant who alleged copyright infringement, had claimed that he met **Ghosh** for a recommendation letter for obtaining the copyright of his script, which was then used in "Kahaani 2".

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court seeks fresh HC hearing after convict flags unfair 20-year bail and reduced prison term - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A man who spent 20 years on bail in a murder case appealed his sentence reduction to the Supreme Court, arguing that his lawyer was not appointed by him and that the amicus curiae did not argue his points. **Justice Dipankar Datta** of the Supreme Court stated that convicts often neglect their appeals while enjoying bail and need to be dealt with firmly. The court found that the convict was not informed about the appointment of the amicus curiae, but noted it would have been desirable for him to be alerted.  The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's decision to reduce his sentence, but directed that courts consider issuing a notice to convicts when appointing an amicus curiae in cases where counsel is absent.

recent_articles.title: How Maharashtra Legislature cleared the Freedom of Religion Bill, and why most of the opposition parties did not oppose it - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Maharashtra** legislature passed the Freedom of Religion Bill, making it the 13th state in India to have such legislation.  While the bill was supported by opposition parties like the Shiv Sena UBT and NCP SP, concerns were raised about its potential infringement on religious freedom and lack of empirical data to justify its need. The bill aims to crack down on forced conversions but has faced criticism from Congress MLA Aslam Sheikh who called it regressive and a one-sided target against a particular community.  **Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis**, however, argued that the current legal framework was insufficient to handle the law and order situation caused by such cases.

recent_articles.title: Jharkhand money laundering case: ED files fifth supplementary Prosecution Complaint involving former Minister Alamgir Alam - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Jharkhand State Rural Road Development Authority
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Directorate of Enforcement (ED)** filed a fifth supplementary Prosecution Complaint against 14 officials from the **Rural Works Department (RWD), Rural Development Special Zone (RDSZ), and Jharkhand State Rural Road Development Authority (JSRRDA)** in Ranchi. The complaint, stemming from an investigation into a bribery racket within these departments, alleges that they collected illegal commissions of 3% from contractors to secure tender allotments.  The **ED** has already conducted 52 searches across multiple states, arrested nine individuals, and seized assets worth over ₹44 Crore in connection with this case.

recent_articles.title: Sara Ali Khan can come to Kedarnath if she submits affidavit that she is Sanatani, says BKTC chief - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hemant Dwivedi**, president of the **Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC)**, stated that actress Sara Ali Khan can visit Kedarnath if she submits an affidavit affirming her belief in "sanatan dharma". The temple committee has implemented a ban on entry for non-Sanatani individuals and restricted mobile phone use within a 50–60 meter radius of the shrines. These measures aim to manage the influx of pilgrims during the yatra season, which saw over six lakh registrations within 11 days.

recent_articles.title: Freedom of Religion Bill passed in Maharashtra Assembly; 'not against any community', says Fadnavis - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra Assembly passed the Freedom of Religion Bill 2026, which prohibits religious conversions through coercion, fraud, or inducement. The bill mandates a seven-year prison sentence and ₹1 lakh fine for those involved in unlawful conversions, with increased penalties for minors, vulnerable groups, and repeat offenders.  **Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis** emphasized the bill's aim to protect citizens from fraudulent conversions while safeguarding constitutional rights. Opposition parties raised concerns about potential "vigilantism" and the bill's impact on religious freedom.

recent_articles.title: SC declines to intervene in Calcutta High Court order for NIA probe into Beldanga violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** declined to intervene in a Calcutta High Court decision allowing the **National Investigating Agency (NIA)** to investigate violence in West Bengal's Beldanga district. The High Court had previously confirmed a trial court order directing the handover of case records to the **NIA**, prompting challenges from **West Bengal** legal counsel who argued against invoking the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).  The **Supreme Court** found the High Court's decision balanced and emphasized the need for impartial consideration of materials in the case.
